STYLE TRANSFER. Picture 1 is a flat, simple vector schematic of a floor plan, drawn exactly to scale (1 metre = 1 square): the third floor of an old 1910 brick apartment building in Ballard, Seattle, seen strictly from directly above with the roof removed. Re-render it completely as a richly textured, hand-painted, realistic top-down map in the style of a professionally published modern-horror map pack. Change the RENDERING of every surface — every flat fill becomes real painted material with grain, wear, dirt and soft shading (wood grain on every board, grout on every tile, iron grating, wet asphalt, fabric, enamel, cast iron) — so that the flat vector look of Picture 1 disappears completely. Change NOTHING of the LAYOUT: it is a surveyor's drawing to be rendered, not an inspiration.

KEEP THE LAYOUT EXACTLY: the position, length and thickness of every wall; every gap in the walls (doorways stay empty openings); the outline and size of every room; the position and footprint of every piece of furniture; the image framing and dimensions. Do not shift, zoom, crop, rotate or re-frame anything. Do not add or remove rooms, walls, partitions, steps, kerbs, low walls or counters, and do not subdivide any room.

Paint NOTHING inside them: no floor, no floorboards, no furniture, no bed, no bathroom, no kitchen, no inner walls, no roof.

The 4 thin dark lines with small square posts are railings (around the fire escape and between the two flights of stairs): keep them thin black iron or wooden railings, never thicken them into walls.

- an outdoor strip at street level, 4 × 20 m, in the middle-left of the image, centred 14% from the left and 50% from the top: dark wet asphalt with shallow puddles, oil stains and cracks, with the folded drop ladder of the fire escape and a dented commercial dumpster and a wheelie bin.
- an outdoor strip at street level, 16 × 2 m, in the upper-centre of the image, centred 62% from the left and 5% from the top: dark wet asphalt with shallow puddles, oil stains and cracks.

Never leave paper, white space or a margin outside the walls.

STYLE: illustrated photorealism like a professionally published modern-horror map pack: crisp, confident dark ink outlines on every wall and every object, filled with realistic painted materials. The walls are thick, solid, matte slate-grey plaster seen only as their flat top edge, with a dark ink outline on both sides. Palette of rainy Seattle in November: wet slate grey, cold harbour blue, deep black; old floorboards in a muted grey-brown (never orange, honey or golden wood, but still recognisably wood); the only saturated colour is a single small crimson accent (the red pins on the wall maps). The map is in COLOUR, not black-and-white: muted, low saturation overall (about 10 to 15 percent), cool, never warm, never golden, never sepia, no green moss.

FLOORS: real materials drawn board by board and tile by tile — long, wide, weathered grey-brown floorboards with dark seams, small white bathroom tiles with grimy grout, scuffed grey linoleum in the kitchen strip, a worn dark runner carpet down the middle of the corridor, steel grating on the fire escape. Seams and joints follow the pattern already drawn in the schematic, so the floor itself reads the 1-metre grid. NEVER draw grid lines, ruled lines or dashed lines over anything.

DETAIL: lived-in and neglected, restrained and legible at table distance: scuffs along the walking paths, grime along the skirting, water stains, a few paper scraps. Outdoors everything is wet from the rain: dark wet asphalt with shallow puddles, rain-darkened concrete, wet tar-and-gravel roofs; but NO falling rain, no raindrops in the air, no rain streaks.

LIGHT AND SHADOW: one flat, even, dim, cold blue-grey ambient light over the whole map, like an overcast sky, the same brightness everywhere: no room is brighter or warmer than another, and the corridor is as dim as the rest. Soft short drop shadows down and to the right under raised objects, and ambient occlusion where walls meet the floor. NEVER paint a light source or its effect: no lit lamps, no glowing screens, no glowing windows, no ceiling lights, no light fixtures, no glowing LEDs, no street lamp, no light pools, no halos, no glow, no lens flare, no bright spots, no beams, no orange light on the ground. Every light is added later by the virtual tabletop.

COMPOSITION: full bleed to all four edges: no border, no frame, no vignette, no paper margin, no white space. Strictly top-down orthographic: walls seen only as their top edge, no wall faces, no ceilings, no perspective, no isometric tilt.

ABSOLUTELY EMPTY OF INHABITANTS: no people, no figures, no figurines, no miniatures, no game pieces, no tokens, no silhouettes, no bodies, no animals, no cars.

DOORWAYS: every doorway is an empty gap in the wall with at most a faint threshold strip on the floor. NEVER draw a door leaf, a door panel, a hinged door, a sliding door or a shutter in any opening, open or closed.

NO MOVABLE FURNITURE: do not add chairs, stools, sofas, tables, floor lamps, rugs, plants, boxes, bags or loose objects that are not in the schematic; they are placed later as separate pieces.

ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT: no letters, numbers, digits, symbols, labels, room names, apartment numbers, signs, logos, writing on the maps pinned to the walls, writing on papers or screens; no compass, no scale bar, no legend.
